verdict: 1/3 as-is, with a clear path to 3/3. I verified the two scariest claims directly in source and both are real: the resume modal (z-index 20) opens behind the opaque loader (z-index 50) while main.ts awaits controller.init() -> offerResume() before ever hiding the loader, so any Stake launch with an active round bricks at boot; and the legal disclaimer's 'Stake Engine' text in info.ts has no data-no-swap guard while sweepDom runs over #m-info with a 'stake -> play amount' mapping, so social mode rewrites the mandatory verbatim disclaimer. Those two plus the $0.00 big-win scenario, the two broken viewports (which the design doc itself names as verified/gated sizes: 320x568 and the 400x225 week-one screenshot gate), and the universal header clip are the six items that fail or brick a review regardless of art quality. The must-fix tier for 3/3 then extends through the reviewer-provokable correctness seams (ungated spacebar, the two pips desyncs, the backward win ticker — all code-confirmed and all in the on-screen-accuracy category Stake screens hardest), the compliance checkboxes the design doc itself commits to (all 12 jurisdiction flags, replay social swaps, the persistent-field contradiction where the mock violates the doc's explicit 'nothing resets between sweeps' contract, per-cluster win floaters, unclipped pay info), and the game-feel layer that separates 2 from 3 stars (static Signal Meter vs the doc's load-bearing detector readout, inconsistent WIN meter vs the doc's 'ticks up, never jumps' rule, the inverted celebration ladder vs the doc's winLevel thresholds, flat big-win staging, stock web-kit chrome vs the doc's two dedicated wooden-UI asset sheets, and the corrupt-looking display font). Two merged findings were cut as speculative for a frontend-only build with mocked math: the present() MODES[mode] casing crash (the audit itself concedes it works on mock math today and the failure requires server book shapes this build never produces) and the auto_close_disabled zero-payout settle deadlock (its scenario requires a config flag not present in this build and its premise contradicts the design doc's stated assumption that the RGS auto-closes zero-payout rounds); both are worth one-line defensive hardening at real-math integration but do not belong on this submission's fix list. Everything ranked 1-21 is must-fix; nothing in it requires rearchitecting math or board logic — it is boot ordering, breakpoints, a swap-table guard, mock-book fixes, presenter bookkeeping, and a celebration/theming pass over systems that already exist.

(2) "Mega spoiled before banner": mock books emit setTotalWin after every paying evaluation (src/mock/bookgen.ts:267) and the presenter ticks the HUD (src/presenter.ts:268-273, src/hud.ts:110-138) — design doc §6 explicitly prescribes this ("Per-evaluation setWin uses the evaluation amount; the end-of-round celebration uses the round total... the win reveal IS the rollup, ticking up through each win"); the banner count-up-from-0 is added drama on top. The issue quotes §6 but inverts its meaning. (3) "$0.00 with x24 lit" (qa/full/p-02-big-mid.png): meter is tag-built multiplier potential; nothing had paid yet, $0.00 is correct. The 03-mega feature capture settled at $11.00 with no banner because rejection sampling returned an 11x book — WIN accumulated normally there too ($11.00 shown from f09 on). Genuine adjacent defect (different issue): off-by-one win tiers in bookgen's winLevelForCents cause a 12.8x round to show MEGA HOARD (qa/full/p-04-mega.png) via presenter's lastWinLevel>=5 gate; worth filing separately.

verifications.corrected_fix: Three concrete changes (all frontend/mock, in scope): (1) src/mock/bookgen.ts:320 winLevelForCents — align to design-doc §6 by shifting every threshold down one tier: x<1→1, x<3→2, x<10→3, x<30→4, x<100→5, x<1000→6, else 7 (current code returns 5 for [10,30), which is the direct cause of MEGA HOARD at 11x/12.8x). (2) src/presenter.ts:296 — change `if (lastWinLevel >= 5 || winX >= 30)` to `if (winX >= 30)` so the end-of-round card is driven purely by round-total-to-bet ratio; the level mapping on line 297 (30/100/1000 → 5/6/7) already matches the doc and needs no change. (3) src/presenter.ts:193-199 setWin case — stop dropping winLevel>=5 evaluations on the floor: play escalated win audio and apply the doc §7 pause (level 5 +2.8s w/ typography card, level 6 +4.5s), so a 44.8x evaluation inside the bonus gets a real beat instead of only the SURVEY-stamp equation line. Optional cleanup: src/winlevels.ts carries a second, conflicting SDK-style ladder (BIG>=25/SUPER>=60/MEGA>=150); only superTextFor is live (>=1000x card text, where it shows 'EPIC WIN'/'MAX WIN' instead of the doc's KING'S RANSOM) — align its names to the doc tier names or delete the dead WIN_LEVELS table. Also note for verification: tools/capture-features.mjs never reaches the end of the trigger bonus (last shot ~46s while the bonus is still running), so extend the tail wait or tap through cards before using those frames as banner evidence.
verifications.notes: Core claim CONFIRMED with hard evidence: qa/features/03-mega-f04.png shows a full-screen MEGA HOARD card counting up an 11x win, and qa/full/p-04-mega.png shows MEGA HOARD at 12.8x — both violate design-doc §6 (MEGA HOARD >= 30x; 10-30x is BIG FIND with no board-covering card). Root cause traced: bookgen's winLevelForCents is off-by-one vs the doc ladder, and presenter's finalWin fires the card on `lastWinLevel >= 5` (book level) in addition to `winX >= 30`, letting the inflated level leak through. The 44.8x half is real but the cited frame is misread: 04-trigger-done is a MID-BONUS capture (equation line still on screen; present() clears it at round end; the -settled shot 12s earlier shows WIN $2.00 mid-bonus), so it does not prove the end-of-round banner never fired — bookgen emits finalWin after bonusSummary and the 46.8x total would have shown a correctly-labeled MEGA HOARD card after the capture window closed. The genuine defect behind that frame is presenter.ts:193-199: per-evaluation setWin handles only winLevel 2-4, so a level-5/6 evaluation (44.8x) gets zero audio/pause/card at the moment it lands, contrary to doc §7's winLevel 5-7 pause rows — spectacle inversion is real in feel. The issue's one-line fix is directionally right but under-specified: driving the END-of-round card off win-to-bet ratio alone fixes the 11x MEGA banner, but without also fixing bookgen's level map and adding the per-evaluation level>=5 beat, in-bonus big evaluations would still read as plain text. Severity 'major' / must-fix is justified: the flagship celebration currently fires at ~1/3 of its doc threshold (any >=10x win), cheapening the entire ladder.

verifications.corrected_fix: The suggested fix is correct and in-scope. In src/presenter.ts, case 'sweepStart' (lines 101-110), reset symbol tracking when the field is reburied. Preferred robust form (matches the existing updateGrid resync pattern at presenter.ts:212-213 and stays correct even for partial refills): after `if (e.refills.length) await this.board.rebury(e.refills);` add `this.tileSym = new Map(this.board.revealedSymbols()); this.recount();` — rebury() sets refilled tiles face-down, so board truth yields exactly the still-revealed tiles. The simpler `this.resetTracking()` also works since bookgen's runBonus always refills all 36 tiles per sweep. No changes to the mock math (bookgen evaluate() is already current-sweep-only and pays correctly); this is purely a presenter/HUD tracking fix.
verifications.notes: Verified end-to-end. Code: presenter.ts sweepEnd (line 234-238) clears the pips DOM only; tileSym/revealedCounts survive across sweeps; resetTracking() runs once per round (controller.ts:197 spin, main.ts:248 replay), never per sweep; sweepStart handler reburies visuals but never clears tracking. Math: bookgen.ts runBonus (lines 496-506) refills all 36 tiles each sweep with revealed=false, and evaluate() (lines 232-241) counts only currently-revealed tiles — so pips and math diverge from sweep 2 onward. Screenshots confirm the on-screen symptom: qa/full/p-06-bonus-sweep.png shows SWEEP 2 OF 10 with only 3 tiles revealed but pips reading 7/8, 5/8, 3/8; qa/features/04-trigger-bigdig-f10.png shows SWEEP 5 OF 13 on a freshly reburied field with an 8/8 hit-state pip. One evidence nitpick: hud.ts:60 caps the display at Math.min(n,8), so it renders '8/8' in hit state rather than literally '9/8' — the substance of the claim (hit-state pip promising a win the evaluation never pays) is accurate. Severity (major, must-fix) is justified: it is a fairness/accuracy display defect during the bonus, the exact category Stake review scrutinizes, though payouts themselves are computed correctly.
